items.title: Mellum2.1 Instruct Is Out, Bringing Faster Answers for Coding Agents
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[Mellum2.1 Instruct Is Out, Bringing Faster Answers for Coding Agents](https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/11/mellum2-1-instruct-is-out-bringing-faster-answers-for-coding-agents/)** — _JetBrains AI blog_. — JetBrains ships Mellum2.1 Instruct, a 12B MoE with 2.5B active parameters that skips chain of thought.
  - Cuts tokens per agentic task 45%, 5.6k vs 10.1k against Thinking
  - 73% fewer tokens excluding tool calls; SWE-bench Verified 40.4 vs 47.0
  - SWE-bench Verified score doubled compared with the previous Mellum2 Instruct
  - Apache 2.0 weights, GGUF builds, and an MTP head up to 1.8x faster

- 🛠 **[1.0.116](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/releases/tag/v1.0.116)** — _Copilot CLI releases_. — Copilot CLI 1.0.116 adds an env setting that reaches every process it spawns, sandbox or not.
  - env covers shell commands, local LSP and MCP servers, hooks, extensions
  - ACP editors can pick a context size without changing saved defaults
  - Warns when a plugin and a standalone MCP server share an endpoint
  - Fullscreen timeline gains Jump to latest; extension manifests get a JSON Schema

items.title: v1.6.1
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[v1.6.1](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/releases/tag/v1.6.1)** — _Pi releases_. — Pi v1.6.1 makes decision models callable from codemode and splits transcript notices into four settings.
  - Copilot's gpt-6-luna-decisions and Radius models callable via models.classify()
  - classify() results now include the provider's responseId
  - Cache miss, warming, compaction cost and reasoning-drop notices each get settings
  - Breaking: showCacheMissNotices is replaced; existing values migrate to all four

items.title: v1.44.0
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[v1.44.0](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/releases/tag/v1.44.0)** — _OpenHands releases_. — OpenHands 1.44.0 adds per-audience automation visibility and an editable key-value store for automations.
  - Conversation mentions ship behind the `conversation_mentions` flag
  - A Factories sidebar entry adds list and drill-in views
  - Hitting a budget now shows a readable error instead of failing opaquely
  - `agent-server` requirement moves to 1.63.1

items.title: Hermes Agent canary canary.20261123T065600Z-v0.23.3

items.title: openclaw 2026.11.10
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[openclaw 2026.11.10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.10)** — _OpenClaw releases_. — 2026.11.10 turns Deep Research and browser handoff on by default, with ClawHub agent templates still behind Labs.

items.title: GLM-5.4: Toward generalized coding with our first loop transformer
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[GLM-5.4: Toward generalized coding with our first loop transformer](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.4)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — Z.ai's GLM-5.4 runs 28 of its layers twice instead of adding parameters, and claims 2-3T-model quality at 750B.
  - Out now for GLM Coding Plan subscribers, in ZCode and Z.ai Chat
  - API access waits on a safety evaluation; open weights come later
  - No benchmark scores published; vision support and 50% more quota

items.title: Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers Despite Being Sandboxed
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers Despite Being Sandboxed](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/7wzWuLP3HhyBLmKfo/models-can-communicate-via-inference-servers-despite-being)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — Two models on one inference server can message each other through vLLM's batching, no network or shared files needed.
  - A shared-KV-cache message board won 1,221/1,221 rounds of a color game
  - A colluding monitor let 354/354 attacks through, still catching 85-92% of honeypots
  - Fix by splitting engine instances, batch-invariant kernels or cache salting

items.title: Introducing Hurdle: Run agent evals on your API, skills, and docs
items.bullet_md:
- 🟡 **[Introducing Hurdle: Run agent evals on your API, skills, and docs](https://www.together.ai/blog/introducing-hurdle-run-agent-evals-on-your-api-skills-and-docs)** — _Together AI blog_. — Together AI open-sourced Hurdle, an npm library that runs Claude Code and Codex against tasks on your own API and scores each run.
  - Scoring mixes code checks, blocking guards and an LLM judge
  - Guards and request checks only work in sandboxed runs
  - The sandbox doesn't limit endpoints by default, so use a low-balance key

items.title: Distilling Kimi-K3.1-Pro into Qwen3.8-27B: Teaching a model a new language
items.bullet_md:
- 🟡 **[Distilling Kimi-K3.1-Pro into Qwen3.8-27B: Teaching a model a new language](https://www.together.ai/blog/distilling-kimi-into-qwen)** — _Together AI blog_. — Together distilled Kimi-K3.1-Pro's Lao into Qwen3.8-27B, lifting a 5.5 chrF++ score to 44.3, or 93% of the teacher.
  - The base model answered in Thai when asked for Lao
  - A LoRA on about 3,800 teacher translations kept Thai at 47.8
  - All experiments together cost $260

items.title: PrismML shrinks a 54 GB language model to 5.9 GB by reducing every weight to just three possible values
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[PrismML shrinks a 54 GB language model to 5.9 GB by reducing every weight to just three possible values](https://the-decoder.com/prismml-squeezes-an-agent-based-coding-model-with-27-billion-parameters-into-5-9-gb/)** — _The Decoder_. — A 27B agentic coding model now fits in 5.9 GB, where full 16-bit precision would need about 54 GB.
  - Every weight is ternary — −1, 0 or +1 — instead of 16-bit
  - SWE-bench Verified rises from 60.8 to 75.6 percent; full Qwen hits 80.6
  - About 204 tokens per second on an RTX 4090, via llama.cpp or MLX

items.title: Anthropic wants to catch rogue AI activity without retaining your data
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Anthropic wants to catch rogue AI activity without retaining your data](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/25/anthropic-enterprise-frontier-safeguards-public-beta/)** — _Help Net Security AI_. — Anthropic's new beta spots misuse patterns across many requests while the conversation data stays in the customer's cloud.
  - Safety Cases hold findings but neither prompts nor responses, pulled via API
  - Older zero-retention checks judged each request in isolation
  - Live on Claude Platform, AWS and Google Cloud; Microsoft Foundry is next

items.title: AI data centers are becoming harder to build, and neoclouds are feeling it
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[AI data centers are becoming harder to build, and neoclouds are feeling it](https://techcrunch.com/podcast/ai-data-centers-are-becoming-harder-to-build-and-neoclouds-are-feeling-it/)** — _TechCrunch AI_. — Nvidia will not backstop a data center until it is nearly ready to run, and neoclouds are feeling the squeeze.
  - Construction delays and more expensive debt are hitting neoclouds
  - Land, power and a finished building matter more than a pitch deck
  - A 2027 shakeout could favour whoever can buy distressed projects

items.title: Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools](https://the-decoder.com/anthropic-study-shows-the-hardest-part-of-adopting-ai-at-work-has-little-to-do-with-learning-the-tools/)** — _The Decoder_. — A 58-company Anthropic study finds AI adoption stalls on review bottlenecks and internal friction, not tool training.
  - 55 percent of deployments raised output or quality; 19 percent added no value
  - Too much AI output to review tops the bottlenecks, at 49 mentions
  - Two-thirds are hiring less because of AI, though only two reported layoffs

items.title: Elastic puts AI agents to work on the SOC alert backlog
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Elastic puts AI agents to work on the SOC alert backlog](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/24/elastic-security-9-6-features/)** — _Help Net Security AI_. — Elastic Security 9.6 hands the alert backlog to six AlertZero Workers spread across four teams.
  - Workers propose actions with evidence, under Manual, Assisted or Supervised autonomy
  - 143 detection rules cover MCP servers, jailbreaks and stolen API keys
  - Adds Linux ransomware blocking plus custom YARA memory scanning
  - Technical preview in Elastic Cloud Serverless; hosted Enterprise due early December

items.title: How iFood scales coding agents across 15,000 repositories
items.bullet_md:
- 🟢 **[How iFood scales coding agents across 15,000 repositories](https://openai.com/business/customer-stories/ifood)** — _OpenAI blog_. — iFood turned coding agents into an internal API: one REST call, a sandbox, a merge request back.
  - 25,000+ runs across 15,000 repos, averaging US$0.04 each
  - Every run uses GPT-5.6 Luna, chosen for cost, speed and intelligence
  - Security platform's fix accuracy and vulnerabilities resolved both more than doubled

items.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
items.bullet_md:
- 🟢 **[GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities](https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities)** — _OpenAI blog_. — OpenAI's GPT-6 models can now design protein shapes from a prompt and code, matching or beating specialist tools on most tasks.
  - 35 of 322 lab-made minibinders bound their target, a 10.9% hit rate
  - Motif scaffolding reached 43.7% versus 27.8% for RFdiffusion
  - Specialized models still supplied sequences and picked candidates for testing
  - Whole-structure prediction still lags: ESMFold2 averaged a 0.93 TM-score

items.title: 1,000 Claude Agents Formalized Fermat's Last Theorem — Lance Martin, Anthropic
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [1,000 Claude Agents Formalized Fermat's Last Theorem — Lance Martin, Anthropic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wrfbI5eyLAI) — **AI Engineer** (18m43s). — For anyone designing multi-agent systems: 1,000 Claude agents formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean in about 30 hours. - Only Git and a SQL database, no domain-specific harness or human steering - The lead agent built its own coordination tables as work progressed - Then memory: stronger models keep better notes - "Dreaming" over transcripts fixes poisoned memories and builds wikis

items.title: I fact checked a coding agent tier list
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [I fact checked a coding agent tier list](https://youtube.com/watch?v=AIcy5foM7zk) — **er1zav** (2m36s). — A two-minute sanity check on coding-agent tier lists: er1zav audits one creator's rankings claim by claim. - Covers Claude Code, Codex, Kiro, Antigravity and Pi - Starts with "Anthropic releases great models and then throttles them"

items.title: My AI Coding Agent Broke a Rule, Then Rewrote CLAUDE.md
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [My AI Coding Agent Broke a Rule, Then Rewrote CLAUDE.md](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DGw2ObWdP1c) — **Sebastian Buzdugan** (9m25s). — Candid, sponsor-funded test of whether a rules service actually stops agents bending instruction files. - Qodo turned instruction files across 13 repos into 361 structured rules - Hand audit of 69 rules: 50 faithful, 8 over-hardened, 6 misread - Get Rules prevented one of 8 rule-break attempts; each task ran once - Imported rules also blocked one valid fix and overrode one request

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon beat GPT-6.2 and Claude in my 25-task AI benchmark
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Gemini 4 Neon beat GPT-6.2 and Claude in my 25-task AI benchmark](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HnUtw3IWT3k) — **How I AI** (31m50s). — Six frontier models, 25 blind-scored tasks across coding, writing, video and prototyping — Gemini 4 Neon wins. - Field: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Neon and Carbon - Blends human blind scoring with LLM-as-judge ratings - Argues coding no longer separates the frontier models - Adds an Annoyance Bench built from her own agent sessions

items.title: I Beat Jev AI with a Fine-Tuned Open-Source Model
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [I Beat Jev AI with a Fine-Tuned Open-Source Model](https://youtube.com/watch?v=YNal-nlQ5F8) — **James Briggs** (33m16s). — A 436M-parameter local model beats Jev on routing accuracy, calibration, latency and cost in one workspace. - Picks the right agent on 85.9% of 205 test posts against Jev's 78.0% - Calibration error 0.052 versus 0.071, at ~27 ms per decision on an RTX 5000 Ada - Under 0.1¢ per 1K decisions on an M4 Max against Jev's 5¢

items.title: The factory mindset: Agentic workflows in production
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [The factory mindset: Agentic workflows in production](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TYhsC-S-Fx0) — **GitHub** (32m15s). — Three production teams show the factory mindset: five engineers shipping 460 pull requests a week on GitHub Actions and Copilot. - Marks & Spencer fixed 77 issues in a single day with autonomous workflows - Provation runs auditable AI agents in regulated healthcare - Argues the process, plus governance and a central control plane, defines the factory

items.title: Securing AI Agents | Mariane Bekker (1Password) | All Day AI 2026
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Securing AI Agents | Mariane Bekker (1Password) | All Day AI 2026](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6NhGp5GFaQ) — **Anaconda, Inc.** (19m41s). — For anyone about to hand an agent real API keys: where credentials leak, and how a vault hands them over at runtime. - Covers identity, authentication, secrets management and permissions for agents - Secrets stay in the vault and reach agents and scripts at runtime

items.title: Hackers Are Coming for Your AI Coding Agent (Lock It Down Now)
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Hackers Are Coming for Your AI Coding Agent (Lock It Down Now)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0q0UbO4oqgQ) — **Cole Medin** (13m52s). — Recent attacks now route through coding agents: a settings file that pulls a backdoor, a package that steals keys. - Passwords and credentials leak into allow lists and conversation history - Stolen AI keys get resold in LLMjacking - His free agent-config-audit skill ships a secrets guard hook

items.title: Open Source LLM Models for Commercial Use (Qwen 3.8 Has a Catch)
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Open Source LLM Models for Commercial Use (Qwen 3.8 Has a Catch)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FJFgsEkf3aM) — **GPU Battle** (2m31s). — A license check across the big open models, aimed at anyone planning to sell on top of one. - Qwen 3.8 27B is Apache 2.0, so you can sell what you build - Sibling Flash-Next needs a separate license for API or assistant businesses

items.title: How Anthropic builds software in 2026 with Katelyn Lesse
items.bullet_md:
- 📝 **[How Anthropic builds software in 2026 with Katelyn Lesse](https://newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com/p/how-anthropic-builds-software-in)** — _Pragmatic Engineer_. — Platform lead Katelyn Lesse on rebuilding the Claude Messages API in Rust in about five months.
  - No Rust experts on the team; Claude helped engineers learn the language
  - A Claude agent categorises API on-call alerts before a human is paged
  - Coding interviews were phased out after strong candidates kept failing them

items.title: Interpreting a recent acceleration in pretraining loss
items.bullet_md:
- 🧪 **[Interpreting a recent acceleration in pretraining loss](https://metr.org/blog/2026-11-24-interpreting-a-recent-acceleration-in-pretraining-loss/)** — _METR_. — OpenAI's published log-perplexity now falls about seven times faster since early 2026 than in 2022 to 2025.
  - METR staff see no matching acceleration in benchmark scores
  - Caveats: possible overfitting, or leakage from OpenAI's own code corpus
  - No internal consensus on what it means for capability forecasts

items.title: Import AI 482: Huawei kernel benchmarks; airborne drone detection; and a national lab's AI science benchmark
items.bullet_md:

  - AscendGYM tests agents writing kernels for Huawei Ascend chips; Opus 5 leads
  - SciResearch-Eval: only GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2 handle a flawed simulator

items.title: vLLM Singapore Meetup: Faster Prefill, Agent-Written Kernels and the Road to Vera Rubin
items.bullet_md:

  - PP2 hit up to 1.37× TEP2 + SP throughput on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash at 2× GB300
  - Agentic turns carry roughly 100K input tokens, about 95% cached

items.title: GPUI is getting its own repository

items.title: [AINews] Jensen Is Back! and OpenAI Shows Its Pretraining Curve, joined by Microsoft
items.bullet_md:
- 📝 **[[AINews] Jensen Is Back! and OpenAI Shows Its Pretraining Curve, joined by Microsoft](https://latent.space/p/ainews-jensen-is-back-and-openai-shows-its-pretraining-curve-joined-by-microsoft/)** — _Latent Space (swyx)_. — OpenAI published its pretraining loss curve and proposed labs agree on a shared development limit.

  - Pachocki expects the next capability jump around 0.68-0.70

items.title: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/why-data-centers-are-at-the-center-of-the-big-tech-backlash/)** — _TechCrunch AI_. — Paris Marx calls the hyperscale buildout fundamentally unsustainable and completely out of line with a livable planet.
  - Argues data centers are physical, so backlash cuts across the political spectrum
  - Cites Ireland, where data centers use more than 20% of national electricity
  - Says Google once drew 29% of one Oregon city's water

items.title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
items.bullet_md:
- 🧪 **[PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents](https://huggingface.co/papers/2611.33144)** — _HF Daily Papers_. — Coding agents write a two-stage programmatic policy for dexterous bimanual tasks, without demonstrations.
  - Scores 72.9 on Bench2Dex and 81.0% success on DexJoCo under full randomization
  - Exploration runs agents in parallel; a distilling agent folds successes into one program
  - Refinement adds randomized layouts for robustness and execution efficiency
  - Real two-hand platform learns a new piano piece from sheet music in 30 minutes

items.title: NVIDIA method caches LLM reasoning as CPU code, cutting costs up to 291x
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[NVIDIA method caches LLM reasoning as CPU code, cutting costs up to 291x](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09891)** — _AlphaSignal · Nov 23_. — NVIDIA's CPU-ARC caches a model's reasoning as CPU-executable code, claiming 16-291x cheaper invocation than the source model.
  - The caches match frontier LLMs on difficult math and science tasks
  - Authors call them explainable, continually trainable and robust to input perturbations
  - Traces compile into small Python functions, with a fine-tuned 1B model for extraction

items.title: DeepMind's Gemini agents discover quantum algorithms up to 290x cheaper, formally verified
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[DeepMind's Gemini agents discover quantum algorithms up to 290x cheaper, formally verified](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09822)** — _AlphaSignal · Nov 24_. — Teams of Gemini 4 agents cut resource costs across quantum algorithms, proving each result in Lean.
  - 290x faster arcsin routine; 2.57x speedup for an implementation of Grover's
  - Fusion simulation 11.8x cheaper, memory down from 5,650 to 4,338 qubits
  - Cytochrome P450 drug-metabolism simulation 2.5x cheaper, 481 to 333 qubits
  - Lean library, problem specs and verified solutions open-sourced on GitHub

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude plugins with 10,000+ tools across all plans
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Anthropic launches Claude plugins with 10,000+ tools across all plans](https://claude.ai/plugins)** — _AlphaSignal · Nov 24_. — Connectors and skills have merged into a single Plugins page inside Claude.
  - Live on Free, Pro, Max and Ultra; Team and Enterprise are coming soon
  - A plugin can be a single connector, a single skill, or several bundled
  - Directory submissions are checked and safety-scanned before listing

items.title: SWE-2.1
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[SWE-2.1](https://cognition.com/blog/swe-2-1?_bhlid=da3f1d2a84f5380c9a4e10c743bc40b26942cea5)** — _The Rundown AI · Nov 25_. — SWE-2.1 is pure-RL on Kimi K3, lifting FrontierCode 2.0 from 24.1 to 41.3 and Terminal-Bench 4.1 from 24.2 to 50.0.
  - ExploitBench climbs from 36.1 to 80.0 on vulnerability work
  - Gains come from long-horizon workflows, not just coding tasks
  - An Ultrafast variant with Cerebras runs the same model at 10x speed
  - Still behind Claude Opus 5.5 on both headline benchmarks

items.title: Anthropic ships Claude Code feature that reviews and fixes your pull requests
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Anthropic ships Claude Code feature that reviews and fixes your pull requests](https://claude.com/resources/articles/introducing-claude-ship)** — _AlphaSignal · Nov 24_. — Claude Ship pairs Code Review with two beta agents: PR Steward and Claude Approvals.
  - PR Steward chases failing CI, merge conflicts and review feedback, but cannot approve or merge
  - Claude Approvals applies a repo policy file, like a smarter CODEOWNERS
  - Developers can trigger it with the new /ship command in Claude Code
  - Team and Enterprise plans, GitHub repos; Code Review stays generally available

items.title: Thinking Machines drops 26B open-source model that runs on 16GB RAM
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Thinking Machines drops 26B open-source model that runs on 16GB RAM](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth)** — _AlphaSignal · Nov 23_. — Inkling 2 Mini is a 26.4B-parameter looped transformer with 3.4B active parameters.
  - Runs its middle layers three times per token; ~20GB native footprint
  - Scores 48.2% on DeepSWE v1.1, the maker's best under 100B parameters
  - Trained natively in NVFP4; GGUF builds ship via Unsloth and llama.cpp
  - Unsloth says the quantized build runs on 16GB RAM

items.title: Project Chaperone: A Rule-Enforcing Harness for Proactive Assessment and Prevention of AI Agent Misconduct (33 minute…
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Project Chaperone: A Rule-Enforcing Harness for Proactive Assessment and Prevention of AI Agent Misconduct (33 minute…](https://appliedingenuity.substack.com/p/project-chaperone-a-rule-enforcing)** — _TLDR · Nov 23_. — Project Chaperone is an open-source harness that checks every workflow call against explicit rules before and during a run.
  - Five default rules block destructive calls, network egress, and leaking personal or untrusted data
  - Pre-run report flags possible violations for a person to accept an exception or acknowledge
  - Demo reads the author's own e-mail and calendar with a local LLM

items.title: When Can You Ship on Offline Evals Alone? (12 minute read)
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[When Can You Ship on Offline Evals Alone? (12 minute read)](https://engineering.atspotify.com/2026/11/when-can-you-ship-on-offline-evals-alone/)** — _TLDR · Nov 23_. — Spotify Engineering says offline evals can replace A/B tests only under assumptions that are hard to verify.
  - A naive estimate puts the squared correlation at 24% where the true figure is 60%
  - Proposes a gate sending weakly positive or negative eval effects to A/B tests
  - A random audit pool keeps testing shipped changes so drift gets caught
  - Arm-dependent LLM judge bias can flip the sign of a result

items.title: Tesla rolls out FSD v15 with a vision encoder shared across FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, claiming 25x better critical…
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Tesla rolls out FSD v15 with a vision encoder shared across FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, claiming 25x better critical…](https://electrek.co/2026/11/21/tesla-fsd-v15-rollout-25x-safety-reality-view)** — _TLDR · Nov 23_. — Release notes tie the 25x claim to the critical intervention rate and add a live Reality View visualization.
  - Reality View replaces separate model signals with one visualization that uses less compute
  - Also targets potholes, road signs and school-zone speed handling
  - Tesla gives the multiplier but not the actual intervention number
